title: Handoff
summary: Writes a full handoff for a fresh session, and suggests one after 2 compactions once the context is 80% full.
benefit: You can move a long task to a fresh session without losing decisions or context.
solves: A session that got too big, and a fresh one that would have to ask you everything again.
use_cases: "write a handoff": the job, every decision, your own words, status and next steps go to ~/.claude/handoffs.
"pass this to session <id>": Claude checks it can reach that session, sends the handoff and checks it arrived.
No target session: you get one start line to paste into a new session in the same folder.
A hook suggests a handoff once a session has 2 compactions and is at 80% of the context.
Background work still running: the handoff is sent right after the last result lands.
details: When you say write a handoff, Claude writes the job, every decision, your own words and answers word for word, the status and the next steps to ~/.claude/handoffs, and can pass it to another session if you give its id. A hook also suggests a handoff once a session has 2 compactions and is at 80 percent of the context. It is for jobs too big for one session. It adds a skill loaded only when used, a Stop hook that checks context after each answer and settings entries; local files only, no network.
trigger: Say "write a handoff" (add a session id to pass it on). A hook also suggests one when context gets big.
verify: d=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1; printf '{"session_id":"verify-1","transcript_path":"%s","scratchpad_dir":"%s"}' "$(cygpath -m "$CLAUDE_SETUP_REPO/tests/fixtures/handoff-transcript.jsonl")" "$(cygpath -m "$d")" | CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=100000 HANDOFF_PROMPT_PCT=0.8 bash "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/hooks/handoff-prompt.sh" | grep -q 'Handoff check'; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $s
risk: A Stop hook checks context size after each answer; the skill writes files under ~/.claude/handoffs. No network.
